cd /home/nab-raj.roshyara@dg-nexolution.de/roshyara/personal/nrna1/docs/knowledgeos/knowlegeos_manual_theory_20261018/06-theory/manuscript; python3 -I - <<'EOF'
p='chapter_01/CH-01-knowledge-authority-execution.md'; s=open(p).read()
R=[
("A later consolidation of 29 open questions sorts them by **what closes them**:\n- **an act alone**: decidable now, for example a naming decision (13 of 29);\n- **another decision first**: two root questions block 11 others;\n- **work not yet done**: an analysis or a completed artifact;\n- **evidence that does not yet exist**: e.g. a second independent execution.",
 "A later consolidation of 29 open questions sorts them by **what they are waiting for before they can be closed**:\n- **nothing**: \"no unresolved dependency; needs only a human act\" [DR L20], for example a naming decision (13 of 29);\n- **another decision first**: two root questions block 11 others;\n- **work not yet done**: an analysis or a completed artifact;\n- **evidence that does not yet exist**: e.g. a second independent execution.\n\nThese are four kinds of **prerequisite**. In the register, the **closing step itself is always an act**."),
("- \"what evidence would close it\" in the paragraph above is too narrow. A closing criterion names **one of these four kinds** of closer, and questions form a **dependency graph**, so whether a question is blocked can be computed;",
 "- \"what evidence would close it\" in the paragraph above is too narrow. A closing criterion should name **what must be in place before the closing act** (nothing, a prior decision, work, or evidence). Questions form a **dependency graph**, so whether a question is blocked can be computed;\n- *Open (different question types):* for a **decision question** (what the organisation will do or adopt), closure is an act. For a **factual or research question**, evidence can *answer* it, but recording that answer as accepted is still an act, because it changes standing. Whether some factual questions may be treated as closed by evidence alone, without an act, is not settled here;"),
("The single compiled contract is \"knowledge feeds authority; it never holds it\" (ARCH-INV-1). It is realized by a type restriction: the verdict enumeration lets a mechanism emit only PASS, FAIL, WARN and INCONCLUSIVE. The values reserved for review acts are excluded by `Verdict::emittable()` (**verified**: `scripts/lib/EngineeringKnowledge/Shared/Domain/Verdict.php` L31–33).",
 "The single compiled contract is \"knowledge feeds authority; it never holds it\" (ARCH-INV-1). It is realized by a type restriction: the verdict enumeration lets a mechanism emit only PASS, FAIL, WARN and INCONCLUSIVE. The values reserved for review acts are excluded by `Verdict::emittable()` (**verified by reading the code**: `scripts/lib/EngineeringKnowledge/Shared/Domain/Verdict.php` L31–33; not tested by execution). *What this establishes, and what it does not:* it guarantees **one boundary** of the invariant, namely that a verdict-emitting mechanism of this library cannot output a review-act verdict. It does **not** establish the whole invariant. Other mechanisms can still produce the effects of authority, e.g. a gate switched to blocking by configuration (§1.14.5)."),
("In particular, a record whose deletion would make a recorded authority act unverifiable, such as the pinned version of the grant behind an exception, cannot be deleted.",
 "In particular, a record whose deletion would make a recorded authority act unverifiable, such as the pinned version of the grant behind an exception, cannot be deleted **while that act may still need to be checked**."),
("*Derivation:* reconstructability (premise R, Ch. 0 §0.5) plus pinning implies retention. **No time-to-live may apply to a pinned referent.**",
 "*Derivation:* reconstructability (premise R, Ch. 0 §0.5) plus pinning implies retention **for as long as the pinning claim may be checked**. No time-to-live may end it earlier. **Permanence does not follow from this alone.** It follows only with a further assumption: that recorded authority acts must remain checkable **indefinitely** (for audit, dispute or history). That is an organisational retention policy, not derived here. The source asserts permanence for its \"governance-critical\" events [DE L406]."),
]
for a,b in R:
    assert s.count(a)==1,a[:50]; s=s.replace(a,b)
open(p,'w').write(s)
open('BASELINE-REVISIONS.md','a').write("""
**Corrections after the Principal's checkpoint review (2026-10-18).** These are derivation defects in the revisions above; the wording was not the issue.

| # | Where | Previous | Corrected | Reason | Type | Impact | Review / decision? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| R1-3a | Ch. 1 §1.4 | "sorts them by **what closes them**"; "a closing criterion names one of four kinds of **closer**"; but also "only an act closes" (inconsistent) | the four are **prerequisites** before the closing act ("needs only a human act", DR L20); closure is an act; factual vs decision questions noted as open | **demonstrated inconsistency** (Principal) resolved from the source | derivation correction | none beyond §1.4 | the factual-question point is open |
| R1-6a | Ch. 1 §1.16.6 | "cannot be deleted"; "**No time-to-live may apply** to a pinned referent" | retention **for as long as the pinning claim may be checked**; permanence needs a further assumption (indefinite checkability) not derived here | overclaim of the derivation (Principal) | derivation correction | a retention policy, if wanted, is an organisational decision | no |
| R1-11a | Ch. 1 §1.9 | "(**verified**: Verdict.php …)" presented as the compiled contract | "verified **by reading the code**; not tested"; establishes **one boundary** of ARCH-INV-1, not the whole invariant | overclaim of what compilation shows (Principal) | derivation correction | none | no |
""")
print('ok')
EOF
python3 -I - <<'EOF'
p='/home/nab-raj.roshyara@dg-nexolution.de/roshyara/personal/nrna1/docs/knowledgeos/knowlegeos_manual_theory_20261018/06-theory/manuscript/BATCH-04-checkpoint.md'; s=open(p).read()
a="| DR decision register | **what closes a question** (act, prior decision, work, evidence); questions form a dependency graph; **answered ≠ closed** | Ch. 1 §1.4 |"
b="| DR decision register | **what a question waits for before closure** (nothing, a prior decision, work, evidence); **closure itself is an act**; questions form a dependency graph; **answered ≠ closed** | Ch. 1 §1.4 |"
assert s.count(a)==1; s=s.replace(a,b)
a="**retention follows from pinning**"; b="**retention for as long as a pinned claim may be checked** (permanence needs a further policy assumption)"
assert s.count(a)==1; s=s.replace(a,b)
a="**realization census** (only ARCH-INV-1 is compiled, verified)"; b="**realization census** (only ARCH-INV-1 is compiled, which guarantees one boundary of it; read in the code, not tested)"
assert s.count(a)==1; s=s.replace(a,b)
open(p,'w').write(s); print('checkpoint ok')
EOF
